title: Introduction to Laboratory Chemistry - Chemistry - Experimental Errors and Data Analysis
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios describes a **systematic error**?
options: Reading a meniscus slightly differently each time due to eye fatigue.
Spilling a small drop of solution on the benchtop.
Using a balance that is improperly calibrated and always reads $0.05\ \text{g}$ too high.
Air currents causing the balance reading to fluctuate.
questions.explain: **Systematic errors** are consistent, reproducible errors in the same direction (always high or always low), often caused by faulty equipment (like an uncalibrated balance) or flawed experimental design.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
Three students measure the density of pure water ($1.00\ \text{g/mL}$) and get the following averages:
- Student A: $0.90\ \text{g/mL}$ (consistent)
- Student B: $1.00\ \text{g/mL}$ (consistent)
- Student C: $1.10\ \text{g/mL}$ (consistent)

Which term best describes Student A's measurements?
questions.explain: Student A's measurements are consistent (implying **high precision**) but far from the true value of $1.00\ \text{g/mL}$ (implying **low accuracy**).
